sections.html:
Wilkes County Tax Administration works out of the county offices at 110 North Street in Wilkesboro. The appraisal department handles revaluation and appeal calls at 336-651-7301, weekdays from 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM. Appeals staff sit on the second floor (see the county's appeals FAQ).

The Tax Administration page pulls the tools together: online payment, a parcel and real property search, GIS maps, personal property forms, occupancy tax information and the Board of Equalization and Review.

  • Listings department: personal property and business listings
  • Appraisal department: assessed value and appeals
  • Online payment link: bills for the current year

The county's last two revaluations were in 2019 and 2025, the newer one effective January 1, 2025. The county estimated that real property values rose about 75% to 80% overall, though the spread was wide. Notices went out on March 17, 2025, showing land and structure values as of January 1, 2025. Owners with present use value land saw both the use value and the gross land value on the notice.

Higher values do not turn into a proportional tax increase, because the county, fire districts and towns set their rates in June. Wilkes also reappraises more often than the eight year minimum state law requires, so ask the tax office when the next one is due before you price a house.

These ranges were estimates made before notices went out, so your own notice and property record are the figures that count. A house in the Town of Wilkesboro and one in the Town of Ronda started from very different places.

The gap is large. Ronda and State Road township sat near 100% or more, while Ferguson township and the Town of Wilkesboro stayed in the 50s. Elkin and Traphill landed at 88% to 93%. If you are selling in one of the faster rising areas, expect buyers to ask what the new value means for their bill, and have the revaluation notice ready.

The area figure explains why a neighbor's notice looked different from yours. It does not replace the sales evidence you would bring to an appeal.

Once a change of value notice reaches you, file the appeal online with your supporting documents. That window closes within weeks of the mailing, so do not wait.

The review period in a revaluation year can stretch to December 1, and hearings may come later. If you have a bill but no decision yet, a later reduction applies back to that year's bill, and a paid bill that gets cut produces a refund.

Filing an appeal does not forfeit the early payment discount. In 2025 the 1.5% discount for paying by August 31 stayed available as long as payment came before September 1, and interest did not begin until January 6.

At the state level, you can ask the county board for a hearing before it adjourns. A Property Tax Commission appeal must be filed within 30 days after the board mails its decision.

The due date is September 1, and a payment made before January 6 carries no interest. From January 6 to February 1 the charge is 2%. After that it is three-quarters of one percent for each month.

The listing period closes January 31 unless the commissioners extend it, and they have pushed back the personal property deadline before. The listings department can give you this year's date. Bills usually go in the mail during the summer.

sections.h2: Paying the bill and the early discount
sections.html:
Wilkes takes payment online through a link on the Tax Administration page, and the tax office can also take it in person at North Street. The bill is due September 1. In 2025, paying by August 31 earned a 1.5% discount, which rewards a seller still living in the house for paying ahead of the due date.

When the house sells before you pay, the balance gets settled at the closing table. Hold on to any online payment confirmation, since the attorney may want it to compare against the county's records.

Three programs run through the Wilkes tax office: an elderly or disabled exclusion, a disabled veteran exclusion, and the circuit breaker deferment. You can pick up an application from the forms page or the tax office. Every year has its own cutoff, so ask early.

  • Elderly or disabled: $25,000 or 50% of appraised value, whichever is larger.
  • Disabled veteran: the first $45,000 of value is excluded, with no age or income test.
  • Circuit breaker: bill limited to 4% of income (5% in the upper band), and the excess becomes a deferred lien.

The Department of Revenue's AV-9 form for 2026 sets an income limit of $38,800. Pick one program, since owners cannot combine them.

Wilkes taxes become a lien on the January 1 listing date, and the buyer's lawyer will want it cleared by closing. Left unpaid, the lien lets the county foreclose and auction the property. Until the sale is confirmed you can still redeem, by paying tax, penalties, interest and costs.

Start with a call to the tax office for the total owed. If a circuit breaker deferral sits on the parcel, tell your closing attorney, because the deferred years come due at the sale.

Results from the revaluation are broken out by four towns, North Wilkesboro, Wilkesboro, Ronda and Elkin, and by township. Inside a town, one bill carries both town and county tax, and a fire district can add its own charge. Rates come from separate boards, so give the tax office your parcel number and ask which districts apply. Buyers in Wilkesboro, North Wilkesboro, Elkin or Ronda will want to see the town portion separated from the county portion, and a rural buyer will ask about the fire district charge instead.

sections.h2: What to ask the tax office before you list
sections.html:
Call 336-651-7301 or visit Tax Administration with the parcel number. The answers decide what your closing attorney holds back from your proceeds.

  • What is the current year's balance, and has the bill been mailed?
  • Is any appeal on the parcel still undecided?
  • Is there a relief program deferral, such as the circuit breaker, on the account?
  • Is present use value land part of the sale?
  • Which fire or town districts apply?

A pending appeal does not pause the bill. Pay by the due date and let any reduction come back as a refund. Wilkes County takes online payment, so save the receipt for the closing file.

1. Ask the tax office to put the payoff figure on paper.
  2. Pass it to your closing attorney along with any deferral details.
  3. Check where an appeal stands so a lower value is not lost.
  4. File away the receipt and the recorded deed.

Selling for cash can shorten the timeline, yet the tax balance still comes out of your proceeds, so the same calls apply.

faqs.q: When was the latest Wilkes County revaluation?
faqs.a: The county revalued effective January 1, 2025, and its previous revaluation was in 2019. It estimated a countywide increase of 75% to 80%, varying by property.

faqs.q: Does an open appeal cost me the early payment discount?
faqs.a: In 2025, no. The 1.5% discount applied if the bill was paid before September 1, even with an appeal pending. Ask the tax office whether a discount applies to the current year.

faqs.q: What happens if the county lowers my value after I paid?
faqs.a: You get a refund of the overpayment. A reduction on appeal applies back to the bill for that year.

faqs.q: Is there an interest-free period on Wilkes County bills?
faqs.a: Yes. Bills are due September 1, but no interest accrues until January 6. After that, 2% applies to February 1, then three-quarters of a percent monthly.

faqs.q: Does Wilkes County give a break to a disabled veteran who owns a home?
faqs.a: Yes. A disabled veteran exclusion removes the first $45,000 of appraised value under state law. File with the county assessor and ask the tax office for the current form.
